assessment: Ten cards to make the width kill on its own. Six are orders, four are in the box. The bench is thirty cards and it is thirty small Vampires: its best four earn slots on their own terms, and the tail loses to the pool because nothing on it triples a token, discounts a Vampire, or turns counters into a flying board. Slots come from cards that serve neither the width plan nor a verified stack. Note what the audit's numbers do not say: interaction reads 12, but Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros all carry removal:damage and Elspeth and Sorin carry removal tags too, so the real answer count is about seven, and protection decomposes to six dedicated slots. This deck is not over-defended; it is over-counted. The bracket floor is 4 before and after every one of the ten.

ten.why: Name Vampire and Preacher of the Schism costs {B}, Welcoming Vampire costs {W}, Bloodline Keeper and Captivating Vampire cost {B}{B}, and an Edgar recast costs {1}{R}{W}{B} — twenty-five Vampires in the 99 and every discount is another eminence trigger in the same turn.
ten.unlocks: Two Vampires a turn from turn four instead of one. Preacher for {B} and Welcoming Vampire for {W} is two eminence triggers; with Anointed Procession and Mondrak on the table that is eight bodies off three mana.

combo_lines_opened.produces: one Vampire cast becomes five creatures entering, five counters on every creature, and flying on the whole board

ten.why: One two-mana Vampire cast through Anointed Procession and Mondrak is five creatures entering, and Cathars' Crusade answers each of them with a +1/+1 counter on every creature you control — then Abzan Falconer, already sleeved, reads those counters and gives the board flying.
ten.unlocks: The alpha strike that does not need Shared Animosity. A board of 1/1 tokens becomes a board of 6/6 fliers off a single three-mana Vampire, on the turn it is cast.

ten.card: Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation // Temple of Civilization

cards: Ojer Taq, Deepest Foundation // Temple of Civilization
combo_lines_opened.produces: twelve Vampire tokens and Purphoros damage per Vampire cast

ten.why: The only tripler in white: one eminence trigger becomes three tokens alone, and layered under Anointed Procession and Mondrak the same trigger is twelve — stack 008 measured the two-doubler version of that board at 10 damage to each opponent per two-mana Vampire, and this is the card that multiplies the number it measured.
ten.unlocks: A 6/6 vigilance body that also triples Legion's Landing, Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror and Bloodline Keeper. Price two things honestly: it is the only pick at six mana and it does raise the maindeck's top end from five, and its death clause returns it from the graveyard as a land — a self-contained line, not an engine, but it is a graveyard clause and the pilot should see it.

ten.closes: Purphoros, God of the Forge (1 card)
ten.why: A fourth token-to-damage payoff for two mana, and the only one that causes life loss rather than damage — so Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles it on your turn, and a five-body eminence cast reads 10 off Corpse Knight alone.
ten.unlocks: Redundancy at the rung the curve wants. The corpus prices it: 5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41% — a fourth copy of the effect that turns width into a clock is the cheapest consistency this deck can buy.

ten.why: Nomad Outpost is one of three lands that enter tapped with no escape, in a deck whose modal mana value is three and whose black is the short colour; Cavern of Souls is the same three colours untapped for the twenty-five Vampire spells, and they stop being counterable.
ten.unlocks: A turn-two Legion Lieutenant off a land that came down on turn one untapped. Land-for-land, so the 37-copy mana base does not move.

ten.why: Once Edgar has attacked, every Vampire token is a 2/2; with Stensia Masquerade out those 2/2s have first strike, so they kill 2/2 blockers and survive, and every one that connects keeps a permanent +1/+1 counter — which is also what Abzan Falconer needs to give the team flying.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod blocks. Against three seats that trade profitably with 1/1 tokens, first strike is the difference between an attack and a chump-block puzzle, and the counters mean the board is bigger next turn even when the attack is answered.

ten.why: Card-advantage reads 4 with a probe note under it naming Castle Locthwain, Minas Tirith, Preacher of the Schism and Midgar, so this is not a count fix — it is a shape swap: Night's Whisper is two cards once for two life, and Bennie Bracks draws at every end step in which you made a token, including the opponents' turns that Charismatic Conqueror answers.
ten.unlocks: Refill billed to the board rather than to your life total, and convoke means the tokens pay for him. Read the limits: he is an Elf Druid so casting him triggers no eminence, and the draw is capped at one per end step.

ten.why: Convoke: tap three Vampire tokens and Markov Baron costs no mana at all, and he is still a Vampire spell, so casting him off the board makes another token — a lord the deck deploys on the turn it is also deploying something else.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the losing hands are the ones with cards and no mana. The argument is the cost, not the anthem — the lord package is eight deep and does not need a ninth at full price.

ten.closes: THE SURVIVING INFINITE (stacks 004 and 006): Bloodthirsty Conqueror
ten.why: Bloodthirsty Conqueror is one card and deck-audit measures the pair that actually kills — Conqueror plus Vito or Sanguine Bond — at 4.8% of games; Forerunner searches a Vampire and puts it on top, which is a fourth way to find the Conqueror that is also a body and an eminence trigger.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod is slow enough that a three-mana 2/2 can spend an ETB looking. Skip it when you would rather have the extra card: it puts the Vampire on top of your library, so it replaces your draw instead of adding to it.

ten.why: Graveyard is covered one card deep by Cemetery Gatekeeper's exile-one-card ETB; Callous Bloodmage's third mode exiles a player's entire graveyard, and when there is no graveyard to hate its first mode makes a Pest — a creature token, so Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros all fire and the doublers copy it.
ten.when: Sleeve it when the pod has a reanimator or a graveyard-value seat; otherwise it is a three-mana Vampire that brings a friend. One caveat the pilot must own: it is on the bench but not in the Vampire scan, so its physical availability is unconfirmed.

acquisition.note: not present in share/Vampire Cards.txt — availability unconfirmed

bench_verdicts.why: Roughly thirty of the ninety-nine cards are black, so the +2/+1 and flying is live under a third of your upkeeps, and {1}{B}{B}{B} is the wrong cost in the colour the audit already calls short.
Protection from black and from red across fifteen tokens ends a game; seven mana in a deck with a modal mana value of three means it ends the ones you were already winning.
A 2/3 deathtouch lifelink body is good rate and it blocks; this deck is the archenemy from turn two and wants the two-drop that makes a token.
Same shape as Gifted Aetherborn one mana later — a defensive flier in a list whose defence is speed, redundancy and resilience, not answers.
A +1/+1 counter on each Vampire is a genuine width payoff, priced at {2} and a sacrificed creature — the exact trade the direction excludes.
Three black mana for Vampire spells off a token is real ramp, and it is ramp that eats the board the deck exists to build.
Two counters per creature death on one equipped Vampire: a death payoff pointed at a single target, and this list wants payoffs pointed at all of it.

bench_verdicts.card: Sorin of House Markov // Sorin, Ravenous Neonate
bench_verdicts.why: Extort drains every opponent with nothing dying, which fits — but the front face is a Human Noble, so casting it makes no eminence token, and the flip is gated on gaining three life in a turn.
Blood tokens are artifacts: Caretaker's Talent draws off them, and Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros do not.

bench_verdicts.card: Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of the Dead
bench_verdicts.why: Five mana whose Bat tokens need opponents to discard lands, with a death clause that returns it from the graveyard — wrong price, wrong direction.
It transforms when you attack with exactly two creatures, and this deck's whole thesis is that it never attacks with exactly two.
Two 1/1 Bats for {2}{B}{B} and exiling it from your graveyard — token production billed to the zone the direction closes.

bench_verdicts.card: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
bench_verdicts.why: The maindeck already runs it as one half of stack 004's verified loop; the bench copy is a spare, not a candidate.
The maindeck copy is pick ten's cut: its Blood tokens do not ping, and its attack trigger puts a Vampire onto the battlefield without casting it, so no eminence.

bench_verdicts.card: Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss, Lord of the Deep
bench_verdicts.why: Outside Edgar's colour identity and unplayable here — sideboard-facts flags it because validate-deck exempts the bench, and it is not in the scan either.
A 1/3 flier gated on gaining two life in a turn before it does anything; the gate is the reason it is off, not the fact that it is missing from the scan.
It draws by sacrificing another creature on attack — a token converted into a card, which is the trade the direction closes.
A 1/4 that makes one Blood token and pays you for sacrificing it; the body blocks and this deck attacks.
A 2/1 conditional first striker whose payoff is a Blood token on death — the eminence trigger is the whole card.
Three mana for a 3/2 trampler that makes a Blood token on connect; the three-drop slot is contested by Stensia Masquerade and Markov Baron.
Five mana for a 4/4 that wants Blood tokens this deck does not manufacture.
Lifelink plus a {2} end-step draw gated on gaining life; Bennie Bracks bills the same repeatable draw to width instead.
It grants deathtouch to one attacker to unlock a mana-sink drain, and the deck's drain already scales with the whole board.
A one-mana white Vampire is a real eminence trigger and this one does nothing else; the curve is not where this deck is short.
A 2/1 flier that cannot block, in a two-drop slot Corpse Knight wants for a payoff.
Intimidate on one target creature per black creature entering; a go-wide board needs evasion on all of it, which is Abzan Falconer's job.

gaps: The interaction reading of 12 against an aggro target of 5-6 is inflated by role tags, not by the decklist. Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Purphoros all carry removal:damage and are the token plan; Elspeth carries removal:spot for her −3 and Sorin carries removal:damage. Read the cards and the deck's real answers are Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Despark, Winds of Abandon, Henrika's edict, Toxic Deluge, Olivia's Wrath and Boros Charm — about seven, two over the band rather than six. Protection decomposes the same way to six dedicated slots. So the ten takes only two slots from protection and one from spot removal; the other seven come from cards that serve neither plan.

No verified line exists for the token kill. Stacks 002, 003, 007 and 008 measure tokens per cast, drain per attack, drain per end step and damage per cast; none is a scenario in which the deck wins. The two lines worth a resolve-stack run are Ojer Taq's tripler layered onto stack 008's two doublers, and Cathars' Crusade feeding Abzan Falconer. Both are declared here as candidates and neither is a fact.

Bloodthirsty Conqueror cannot be given redundancy from this pool. It is the only card left that reads 'whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life', and the pool's four openers against it — Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric, Cliffhaven Vampire and Vizkopa Guildmage — are all third and fourth copies of the lose-half the deck already has two of. Forerunner of the Legion finds the Conqueror; nothing replaces it.

The obsolescence index produced no usable claim. Its 17 hits include Scrapwork Mutt and Fear of Missing Out 'upgrading' Cemetery Gatekeeper, Hoofprints of the Stag and Wedding Announcement 'upgrading' Caretaker's Talent, and Mister Gutsy 'upgrading' Cordial Vampire; read the oracle text and none of the five makes a Vampire, a token on cast, or an anthem this deck can use. No obsoletes claim is made in the ten.

The synergy graph could not be used either. Its 25 pool candidates are 25 Auras sharing the identical five 'Aura + Protection' partners, and nine of the ten picks have no in-deck partner on their own shortlist at all. That is a rule artifact, not a lead, and no synergy_partners_in_deck claim is made.

The ten raises the cost of the slots it touches. The nine nonland adds average 3.6 mana against 2.6 for the nine they replace, in a deck whose curve the audit reports at a modal mana value of 3. Urza's Incubator and two convoke costs (Markov Baron, Bennie Bracks) are the hedge; re-running goldfish after the swap is the only way to price it.

goldfish_targets.json declares 'An answer to a noncreature permanent drawn (the binding axis)' over exactly one card, Cemetery Gatekeeper, whose text exiles a card from a graveyard and answers no permanent. Despark is the deck's noncreature answer and sits outside the group. The 16.6% is measuring the graveyard class under a label about permanents; a goldfish re-derivation settles it.

sideboard-facts reports no EDHREC rank for any of the thirty bench cards, while cards.csv carries one for every one of them (Stensia Masquerade 5555, Markov Baron 3552, Forerunner of the Legion 5952, Callous Bloodmage 7788). The ranks quoted here come from cards.csv, and none of the three scanned bench picks was chosen on popularity — sideboard-facts is right that the argument has to rest on the deck's own needs.

Cavern of Souls' colour contribution cannot be computed. manabase.land_colors is restriction-aware and Cavern's coloured mana is spendable only on Vampire creature spells, so no colour-source delta is claimed for it — and it does not cast Despark or Boros Charm, which Nomad Outpost did. The diagnosis's standing gap on black's true source count is unchanged by this pick.

Callous Bloodmage is on the bench but absent from share/Vampire Cards.txt, so its availability is unconfirmed and the pilot should check the box before ordering the other six. The other two unscanned bench cards are off the list for reasons that make availability moot: Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss is outside the colour identity, and Scheming Silvertongue's lifegain gate fails on its own.
